bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geographical concentration in Gujarat and adjoining regions — A significant part of the Company's operations and business presence continues to be concentrated in Gujarat and adjoining regions, exposing it to regional market and regulatory conditions.
- Working capital intensity of EPC and project development — Solar EPC and project development activities require significant upfront expenditure and working capital, which may pressure liquidity and cash flows during periods of rapid business expansion.
- Land-related execution risk — Ground-mounted and utility-scale solar projects require suitable land, and identification, acquisition, leasing and statutory approval of land can involve considerable time and execution complexity.
- Dependence on project execution across multiple stages — EPC projects involve multiple stages, vendors, regulatory approvals and customer dependencies; delays at any stage may affect project timelines and working capital cycles.
- Increasing competitive intensity — The solar EPC market is becoming increasingly competitive with large established companies as well as regional and smaller players, and competitive pricing may exert pressure on project margins.
- Regulatory and policy risk — Changes in Government policies, subsidies, incentives, renewable purchase obligations, net-metering and open-access regulations, tendering frameworks and grid connectivity requirements may affect project economics, demand and execution.
- Supply-chain and equipment price volatility — Fluctuations in the prices and availability of solar modules, cells, inverters, electrical equipment and other critical components may affect project costs, margins and execution schedules.
- Financing and interest-rate risk for capital-intensive IPP projects — Changes in interest rates and availability of project finance may influence the affordability and financial viability of renewable energy projects, particularly for capital-intensive IPP projects.

outlook.body:
- Transform from a solar EPC company into an integrated energy company spanning project development, EPC, energy storage and ownership of renewable energy assets.
- EPC: strengthen the core EPC business and selectively participate in large-scale solar, hybrid and government renewable energy projects.
- IPP: build and operate a diversified renewable energy portfolio to create a base of recurring long-term revenues.
- BESS: establish a position in energy storage, serving applications from residential and commercial systems to utility-scale projects, via acquisition of a controlling stake in Zenwatt Clean Energy Private Limited.
- Integrated Energy Projects: develop integrated solar parks and Wind-Solar Hybrid parks combining generation, storage and transmission infrastructure.
- Focus on strengthening project execution capabilities, optimising procurement and supply-chain processes, improving operational efficiencies and maintaining disciplined working-capital management.
- Adopt a prudent, disciplined approach to project selection, risk management and capital allocation as the Company scales and diversifies.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Zodiac Energy is expanding its Independent Power Producer (IPP) portfolio, with approximately 320 MW operational IPP capacity and a further 60 MW in the pipeline, targeting approximately 400 MW by end of FY 2028-29. The Company is entering the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) market via acquisition of a controlling stake in Zenwatt Clean Energy Private Limited, targeting BESS manufacturing from residential/commercial to utility-scale applications. It is also developing integrated Wind-Solar Hybrid parks and pursuing large-scale government renewable energy projects, building on the commissioning of a 38 MWp (DC) / 30 MW (AC) solar project for the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation. During FY2025-26 the Company acquired controlling interests in several solar-project LLPs (Radhavallabh Solar Projects LLP to 98%, Priyapritam Solar Projects LLP to 98%, Dharmik Solar Projects LLP to 51%, Shamli Solar Projects LLP to 98%) and disposed of its entire interest in Dhwarkesh Solar Projects LLP.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's renewable energy sector continues to offer significant long-term growth opportunities, supported by increasing energy requirements, transition to cleaner electricity, and Government initiatives.
- Continued expansion of solar capacity, increasing adoption of rooftop solar, and growth in commercial and industrial demand are expected to provide opportunities for business growth.
- Government-led programmes, including PM-KUSUM and rooftop solar initiatives, are expected to create opportunities wherever commercially and operationally viable.
- The growing IPP segment is expected to complement the EPC business by providing long-term revenue potential and greater earnings visibility.
- Emerging developments such as energy storage, hybrid renewable energy systems and digital monitoring are expected to create additional opportunities across the value chain.
- The industry is expected to become increasingly competitive, requiring strong execution capabilities, efficient supply-chain management, financial discipline and technological adaptability.
